assumptions: All auxiliary alphabets are finite, with infeasible families interpreted using the claim’s extended-real convention.
The imported converse theorem is assumed valid only in the form represented by the accepted claim.
The nested optimizations are performed in the stated order and are not exchanged.

facts.condition: Provided the imported converse theorem is sound, removing its common-message coordinate yields a finite constraint model for the canonical two-private-message task. Coupling the auxiliary receivers contributes no further constraint information once each receiver’s input-conditioned channel is fixed.

When the optimization nesting specified by the accepted claim is retained, the specialized constraint model supplies a converse ceiling for the combined private rates of the canonical broadcast channel.

rootContract.objective: Determine the exact private-message sum-capacity C_sum of the half-skew binary skew-symmetric broadcast channel specified by the canonical problem.

referenceCommunity.description: A counterfactual community of competent human mathematical researchers collaborating on the canonical BSSC objective, with its program and thread portfolio defined exclusively by the bound builder-v6 knowledge projection.
referenceCommunity.researcherQualification: For each local work package, a researcher with graduate-level mathematical maturity and the information-theory, probability, optimization, or computer-assisted proof expertise needed to begin productive work without general disciplinary training, but without unpublished solution-specific knowledge.

rootContract.terminalCondition: A validity-v4 accepted result establishes one exact value of C_sum by matching rigorous achievability and converse bounds, including every limiting, cardinality, and certification condition needed for the canonical channel.

workUnit.definition: One focused person-hour of research by a researcher qualified for the relevant work package, using the fixed conventional tool baseline named by this contract.
workUnit.toolBaseline: Public mathematical literature and standard non-autonomous research tools available as of 2026-08-25, including handwritten reasoning, symbolic algebra, numerical computation, interval arithmetic, proof assistants, and code execution on commodity research hardware; autonomous LLM or agent labor is excluded.

updates.rationale: The manifested submission makes the auxiliary-receiver route a credible, frequently relevant converse program by supplying an exact premise encoding, specialization framework, product-marginal reduction, and audit tool. Remaining program-level work is primarily synthesis with the canonical BSSC objective and coordination of unresolved optimization and certification tasks.

Researchers will often need to formulate and sequence the remaining receiver optimization, numerical-bound, cardinality, limiting, and comparison tasks. The submission explicitly identifies these unresolved boundaries, so agenda work remains moderate.

Access to the complete submission leaves little reconstruction work in this package: it supplies the R0=0 expansion, all 30 independently generated rows, the exhaustive output-term audit, and the input-only product-marginal reduction. A small amount remains for local checking and integration.

Substantial exploratory work may still be required because the submission does not determine the Q0-supported optimum, a numerical converse value, receiver cardinality, coercivity, continuum limits, or matching optimality. The structured foundation reduces setup cost but not these difficult downstream searches.
